additionalCoursework: Biochemistry is strongly recommended. Genetics, Cell Biology, and Microbiology are recommended if the applicant's undergraduate program of study permits.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: Mercer University School of Medicine is a welcoming community reflective of the State of Georgia and the United States of America.  Please visit https://medicine.mercer.edu/about-the-school/vision-mission-and-values/
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: MUSM has the following categories for Leave of Absence: Maternity/Paternity Leave of Absence; Child Care and Caregiver’s Leave; Personal Leave of Absence; Medical Leave of Absence; and Mandatory Medical Leave of Absence. The student must request the associate dean of academic affairs permission to re-enter the program at least 2 weeks prior to the requested reentry date.  The full policy is contained in the MUSM MD Program Handbook.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: 4-year campuses in Macon, Savannah, and Columbus, Georgia.  Beginning with the Class of 2029 the final two years will be available in Valdosta and Carrollton, Georgia
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Please visit http://residencelife.mercer.edu/macon/graduate-housing.cfm for information.  Most medical students live close to their campus.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: Mercer University School of Medicine supports all of its students of each campus.  To learn more about our Students Affairs Offices and programming, please visit our website: https://medicine.mercer.edu/student-affairs-and-services/.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: Wellness is considered critical to student life and various programs are available.  The Office of Student Affairs can be reached at: https://medicine.mercer.edu/student-affairs-and-services/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: This varies with location.  The primary difference is that Macon is the location of Mercer University and thus provides the university environment for medical students.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: We have a dress code and students are expected to adhere to it.  It is available at: https://medicine.mercer.edu/student-affairs-and-services/
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: All faculty have an open-door policy, but if the faculty member is unavailable at that time appointment will be scheduled at the earliest convenience for the student and faculty member.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Year 1 onward.  We have an extensive network of Standardized Patients for facilitating learning of basic clinical skills.  Community based clinical experiences also start late in Year 1.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: The Year 1 and 2 curriculum primarily uses a case driven approach in the basic sciences in small groups (7-9 students); this is led by a tutor who is a faculty member.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: MUSM does not directly report class rank. Performance relative to peers in clerkships, etc. is reported in the Medical Student Performance Evaluation Letter in accordance with recommended guidelines.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Attendance in most sessions is mandatory.  Lectures may be made available by some faculty prerecorded for streaming by students on demand through the learning management system.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The curriculum, which is guided by the school's mission, is designed to provide a general professional education that prepares students to enter into and excel in graduate medical education in any specialty.  The curriculum is competency-based and is guided by objectives that fall into the competency domains of: medical knowledge, patient care, practice-based learning and improvement, interpersonal and communication skills, professionalism, and systems-based practice. The curriculum is integrated in multiple respects - the basic sciences curriculum is case-based; instruction in clinical skills begin in the first year; students begin to have patient care experiences in a clinical and community setting as early as the first year.  

The curriculum is student-centered, challenging, encourages and sustains active engagement and participation of students in the learning process and the object of study.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: The mission of Mercer University School of Medicine (MUSM) is to educate physicians and health professionals to meet the primary care and health care needs of rural and medically under served areas of Georgia.   The six core primary care specialties are Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, General Surgery, Obstetrics & Gynecology, and Psychiatry.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms:
Medical students at MUSM have opportunities to participate in basic, clinical, or translational research. First-year medical students are encouraged to participate in the Summer Scholars program in the summer between their first and second years. All students who wish to engage in research opportunities are given that opportunity.  Opportunities are also available for third and fourth year medical students to work on clinical or translational research projects. 

Fourth year medical students can continue a research project by taking a special topics elective.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: The Admissions Committee considers an applicants record of service to the community in its evaluation of applicants.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: Continuously updated information about research and service opportunities is available from the Director of the Working Group on Student Research and Service Opportunities.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Mercer University's School of Medicine was established in 1982 to educate physicians and health professionals to meet the primary care and health care needs of rural, medically underserved areas of Georgia. Approximately 65 percent of MUSM MD graduates practice in the state of Georgia.  All applicants to the MD Program must be legal residents of the State of Georgia.

The curriculum provides a general professional education that will prepare students to enter into and excel in graduate medical education in any specialty. The curriculum is competency-based and is guided by objectives that fall into the competency domains of medical knowledge; patient care; practice-based learning and improvement; interpersonal and communication skills; professionalism; and systems-based practice.  The curriculum emphasizes self-directed and active learning methods, including the use of small tutorial groups and a case-based format for learning biomedical sciences in the context of their application.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The mission of Mercer University School of Medicine (MUSM) is to educate physicians and health professionals to meet the primary care and health care needs of rural, medically underserved areas of Georgia.
medSchoolInformation.programUndergradCollege: This program is limited to Mercer University Undergraduates who are invited to apply to the program.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: This is a new "3+1" program that allows selected Mercer University undergraduate students to enter Mercer University School of Medicine after three years provided they meet program academic and professional requirements.  Completion of the first year of medical school will result in the awarding of the degree Bachelor of Science.

medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Applicants will have no more than 2 weeks to indicate if they accept the offer, otherwise the offer may be withdrawn.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
The types of letters that can be sent to AMCAS on an applicant’s behalf include: committee letter, letter packet, or individual letter.  Applicants who have committee letters submitted may also have additional letters submitted up to the limit of eight (8).

As a general rule, letters of recommendation should be sought from referees who know the applicant well as a student, coworker, colleague, or employer. When possible, we recommend that at least one letter of reference be submitted from a science faculty member who has taught the applicant and that at least one letter of recommendation be submitted from a physician, healthcare professional, or health care manager with whom the applicant has had a mentor-mentee, employment, or volunteer relationship.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: The second week of July for Early Decision applicants and late-August for Regular Pool applicants.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: One 45-minute interview with two interviewers, one of whom will be a member of the Admissions Committee.  There will also be a subsequent one-hour group session for with three second-year medical students following the primary interview.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: Introduction, interviews, and group discussions are held on Tuesdays and Thursdays from approximately 10:00 to 12:15 pm.  All interviews will be virtual (on Zoom) for the 2026-2027 Admissions Cycle.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews will be conducted by video (on Zoom) for the 2026-2027 Admissions Cycle.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Applicants meeting a minimum MCAT percentile + Cumulative Undergrad BCPM GPA. MCAT score must be from April 2021 or later.
medSchoolApplication.secApplEarliestDtText: Secondary application can be submitted upon invitation.
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: Deadline is on or about January 12, 2027.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: Applicants must be legal residents of the State of Georgia and must be US citizens or Permanent Residents.  There are no exceptions.  Permanent residents must be on the path to US citizenship.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo:
MUSM does not average MCAT scores. We use the applicant’s highest MCAT score to determine secondary application eligibility. At least one MCAT score must be from a test taken after June 30, 2023.

Applicants who retake the MCAT after submitting an application are allowed to note additional intended MCAT test dates on their Primary AMCAS Application.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: MCAT minimum is a 25th percentile, which varies slightly from year to year.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: All applications are reviewed holistically, meaning that all components of the application are taken into consideration during the review process.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: The applicant must have taken the MCAT at least once on or after April 1, 2026, and obtained a percentile rank of at least 31. A scalar product of BCPM GPA*MCAT Percentile of at least 93 is required to receive an invitation to submit a secondary application.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: For applicants with earned graduate degrees or 20 or more credit hours of graduate coursework, an invitation to submit a secondary application is sent if the average MCAT percentile rank is 25 or greater, regardless of Cumulative Undergraduate BCPM-GPA.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept community college credits that meet our admissions criteria. For more information visit: https://medicine.mercer.edu/admissions/doctor-of-medicine/admissions-process/
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Applicants are limited to ONE letter in each category and these must be submitted as a pdf.  Other formats, e.g., body of an email message are not accepted.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Applicants must meet our technical standards prior to matriculation.  These are provided by the Office of Student Affairs

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
Financial aid in the form of loans and scholarships is available to eligible accepted students. Most scholarships are based on need and mission compliance.  Financial need is determined by a federally approved need analysis formula.  

For further information, please visit the MUSM Office of Financial Planning at: http://medicine.mercer.edu/student-services/financial-aid/
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition for all students is due on the first day of class for each semester.  The full tuition policy can be found at http://bursar.mercer.edu/macon

medSchoolPrograms.info: A new "3+1" program that allows selected Mercer University undergraduate students to enter Mercer University School of Medicine after three years provided they meet program academic and professional requirements. Completion of the first year of medical school will result in the awarding of the degree Bachelor of Science.

MUSM offers a 1-year graduate degree program, the Master of Science in Preclinical Sciences Program (MSPCS), on the Macon Campus. This is not a traditional postbaccalaureate program.  Applicants must have already taken the standard prerequisites for medical school, including general biology, general chemistry, organic chemistry, and physics.  The goal of this program is to enhance the scientific knowledge of graduates in the fundamental sciences foundational to medicine (biochemistry, microbiology, cell biology, immunology, physiology, and human development).  More information is available here: http://medicine.mercer.edu/admissions/preclinical/

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: One-year laboratory courses in general biology, general or inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, and general physics from an accredited institution are required. Laboratory requirements may not be completed online beginning with the 2025-2026 application cycle unless they were completed during interruptions caused by COVID-19. Offers of acceptance are contingent upon the receipt by Mercer University School of Medicine of official transcripts of all post-secondary course work including fulfillment of required premedical courses by June 30 of the expected year of matriculation.  Other courses that are not required but are strongly encouraged include introductory or upper level courses in biochemistry, mathematics, cell biology, immunology, histology, genetics, molecular biology, behavioral science, and humanities.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: Prerequisite courses do not expire if taken at an accredited institution in the US.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Complete information about eligibility criteria for applying, dates and deadlines can be accessed from links at https://medicine.mercer.edu/admissions/doctor-of-medicine/. The overarching goal of the admissions process is to identify and enroll well qualified students who are likely to become caring and well-rounded physicians, committed to serving the primary care and healthcare needs of rural, medically underserved areas and populations in Georgia.  MUSM accepts applications to the MD program only from US Citizens or eligible non-citizens (i.e., permanent residents of the United States).  Applications are accepted only from applicants who have established domicile at least 12 months prior to the expected date of matriculation and maintain domicile in the state of GA at the time of submitting a Primary Application.  Admissions policies are subject to revision.  For the most recent information, please visit https://medicine.mercer.edu/admissions/doctor-of-medicine/
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: No specific recommendation.  We evaluate applicants holistically and have a broad concept of what counts as "shadowing" experience.  Applicants are expected to have a significant record of service to others and their community.
